apple_photo.1: Apple MakerNotes, depth data, the HDR gain map and MPF images are proprietary and not part of the preset.
apple_photo.2: Exposure time, ISO, brightness and focus area differ for every shot — the preset does not invent them (they can be set manually).
apple_photo.3: ColorSpace is not taken from the preset: it follows the ICC profile actually embedded in the result (iPhone: Display P3 + “Uncalibrated”; an sRGB file gets “sRGB”).
apple_photo.4: A real iPhone shoots HEIC by default; the preset describes the JPEG variant (“Most Compatible”). The camera never creates PNG/WebP with camera EXIF.

samsung_photo.1: Samsung MakerNotes, the Samsung trailer (Motion Photo, capture data) and the Ultra HDR gain map are proprietary and are not copied.
samsung_photo.2: Samsung's ImageUniqueID is an encoded camera-module identifier with an unknown structure; it is not part of the preset.
samsung_photo.3: Exposure time and ISO differ for every shot — the preset does not invent them (they can be set manually).
samsung_photo.4: ColorSpace follows the ICC profile actually embedded, not the preset.
samsung_photo.5: The Model field depends on the firmware: recent firmware writes “Galaxy S2x”, older firmware writes the SM-… code.

how.1: ExifTool writes the EXIF/XMP/QuickTime fields; FFmpeg writes the container structure (brand, track handlers, timecode, codec).
how.2: After writing, every file is read again with ExifTool and compared with the profile; mismatches go to the log.
how.3: ColorSpace, image dimensions and frame rate come from the real file, not from the preset.
how.4: Presets never write GPS or any other location data.
how.5: Rewriting tags does not reproduce the full “fingerprint” of a camera or editor: the encoder, stream parameters and proprietary structures stay different.
